title: Learning from my mistakes
author: Nifefiend
selftext:
I posted a few weeks ago about my first experience trying to build a video game in Godot using free ChatGPT. I learnt a lot and one of you gave pretty straightforward feedback about how to do it properly, with a readme for agents to understand and setting up a GitHub.

  
So I spent a few weeks outlining the high level game design, specifications, features and environment. Then i went back and forth with ChatGPT about what was missing, what might be interesting and built it out some more.

  
Yesterday I bought Claude Pro, setting up the skills, spent time getting the architecture, discussing underlying elements and GitHub set up and then started building and the end result is the start of a prototype.

The better AI is obviously making a difference but asking it to pretend to be a Video Game Lead Designer and building the game feature by feature in a logical order is making a huge difference. I explained that I am not a coder and its explaining what its doing and why every step of the way. I'm sure that's going to use extra tokens but that's fine by me.

I don't know how far i'll take it but as a side hustle for £18 a month, I am having fun. Reminds me of messing around with Warcraft 3 World Editor

What i've build so far:

* Core mechanics of reclaiming the land
* Planting and growing trees
* Animals with jobs and day/night cycles
* Base water mechanics
* Base building mechanics

comments.author: james6626
comments.body: The most important thing is to persevere!! Best of luck!
